study type: Prospective observational comparative study (case series compared to retrospective cohort with matched-pair analysis)
exposure: Vaginal breech delivery in all fours position
Vaginal breech delivery with classic support
outcome: Transfer rate to neonatal intensive care unit
cohort: The study included mothers undergoing vaginal breech delivery at a single center, with a prospective group delivering in the all fours position and a retrospective group receiving classic support.
finding: Vaginal breech delivery in the all fours position is a feasible non-interventional method that significantly reduces maternal perineal injuries, but it is associated with increased newborn prenatal hypoxic stress, though without observed clinical consequences for the neonates.
mod_finding: Vaginal breech delivery in the all fours position significantly reduced maternal perineal injuries (14.6% vs. 58.5%) but led to increased newborn prenatal hypoxic stress (lower pH and base excess) compared to vaginal breech delivery with classic support.
